results.name: Lowpoly Rocks - 1
results.description:
A collection of reprocessed rocks and stones ([other free assets here](https://skfb.ly/6yQSW)), ready to use as game props, particles or for optimized renderings. Just don't pretend they're yours or try to resell them. Any feedback is welcome!

Each model is made of 500 triangles, and 1024 pixels albedo and normal maps.

The original scans were remeshed with [mmgs](http://mmgtools.org), and decimated, UV unwrapped and baked in blender. Normal maps are ready to use for Unreal Engine, but don't forget to flip their green channel in Unity!

Special credits to @3dhdscan and @reductio for their very nice scans, and also to @quintessenz, @saschahenrisch, @dqh18, @struffelproductions, @calidos, @archaeo3d, @kudo, @not_lonely, @demidroid, @suramis and @baptisteberard.

All original models licensed under CC attribution.

 

*particle system example*

![Imgur](https://i.imgur.com/W3H8eG6.jpg)

results.name: PetStock and Radio Rentals Building (low Poly)
results.description:
This asset is a replica of the PetStock and Radio Rentals retail in Preston, Victoria, Australia
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2767004544

PETstock is a family-owned and operated business that started in 2002 in regional Victoria, 11 years after the Young family took ownership of Ballarat Produce in 1991. Over the past 16 years, Brothers David and Shane have grown the business into the second-biggest specialty pet retailer in Australia, after Greencross Limited’s Petbarn.

Radio Rentals was formed by Percy Perring-Thoms in 1930 in Brighton, Sussex, UK to rent out radio sets as well as offering televisions and video recorders for rent in later years. In 1939, the business expanded into Australia with the first shopfront opening on Market Street, Sydney in 1937. The company now operates over 90 Radio Rentals stores within Australia, and 28 stores in New Zealand.

results.name: Michaelsoft Binbows Building (low poly) マイケルソフト
results.description:
This asset is a replica of the Michaelsoft Binbows store intended for Cities Skylines.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2842768620

"Michaelsoft Binbows" is an obscure Japanese store which sold used PC and computer parts with a name parodying  Microsoft Windows. The store was closed sometime around early 2002 and has never been reopened as Michaelsoft Binbows. 
The original building can still be found today at Koaigimachi, Maebashi City, Gunma in Japan.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

このアセットは、Cities Skylinesのために作られたマイケルソフトビンボウズストアのレプリカです。

「マイケルソフトビンボウズ」は、Microsoft Windowsをパロディ化した店名で、中古のPCやPCパーツを販売していた日本の無名店です。この店は2002年初めに閉鎖され、その後、マイケルソフトビンボウズとして再開されることはありませんでした。
現在、群馬県前橋市小合町に当時の建物が残っています。

results.name: Brooklyn Street Twin Buildings Low Poly
results.description:
**Authentic low poly urban model featuring two adjacent buildings, including a distinctive corner building. Both structures showcase storefronts on the ground floor, ideal for creating lively city streets and commercial districts in game environments or real-time visualizations. Designed with optimized geometry and detailed facade textures to ensure smooth performance and immersive realism.**

**Model information:**

* **Format: glTF**
* **Vertices: 4,325**
* **Faces: 2,774**
* **Triangles: 6,026**
* **Textures(3): BaseColor, Roughness, Metallic**
  
**P.S. If you have a problem with the material transparency, go to the material settings -> find the render method (or blend mode) -> change it from "Blended" to "Dithered". This fixes many alpha channel issues like inside-out or invisible faces.**

**Feedback is welcome!**
